reference.notes:
I've implemented the spec in `packages/core/src/selection/`, and every test passes. The `categories.*` suite passes 82 of 82, `hidden-categories` passes 113 of 113, and the whole package suite passes 219 of 219, with `tsc` compiling cleanly. Only files in that folder changed, and every exported name and signature is the same as before.

- **`facts.ts`**: `factsFor` turns one Jira issue into `IssueFacts`:
  - Ages are whole days and never negative.
  - Due dates and release dates are counted as calendar-day differences in UTC from the first ten characters of the date, and are null if those characters aren't a real date.
  - Priority, issue-type and link-type names are trimmed and lowercased before matching. Priority is looked up only among the table's own keys, so names like `"constructor"` or `"__proto__"` rank `"none"`.
- **`rules.ts`**: `evaluate` walks the rule tree. `all` stops at its first child that doesn't match; `any` checks every child. A signal's `describe` runs only after its test passes. Clauses keep their order, with blanks and duplicates removed, and are empty when the rule doesn't match.
- **`signals.ts`**: All the factories share one threshold check, so a negative or non-finite value throws a `RangeError`.
- **`categories.ts`**: The six rules are built exactly as in the spec's table. Board overrides are read only from the board's own keys, and unusable values fall back to the defaults. `createClassifier` checks ids and builds each enabled rule once, when it is created, and `classify` is `createClassifier(...)(facts)`.

One wording in the spec could be read two ways: `deadlineWithin` "describes the nearer of the two". I took "nearer" to mean the date with fewer days left, counting overdue as negative, with ties going to the due date. Reading it as the date closest to today could describe a deadline outside the window while the other date is what made the issue match. Every test that touches this agrees with my reading.
